Award: "Ace of act" from Act Snowboarding, scored 19.0/20 (2020 model) [44] 113. Review style classification: All-Mountain-Freestyle (Snowboarding Profiles) [3] 114. Review price referenced: $669 (Snowboarding Profiles) [34] 115. Carving performance: "Can carve pretty well for a twin but it isn't a super carver" [35] 116. Powder performance: "Floats pretty good for a twin and there is a lot of nose/tail" [35] 117. Switch riding: "Pretty much the same either way" — true twin [35] 118. Speed performance: "All that nose and tail starts to feel like you are running with clown shoes on if you really point it and the vibrations can get between the feet" [35] 119. Edge hold: "Decent edge hold but it let go pretty quick" in harder snow conditions [35] 120. Buttering/flex: "Very poppy where the camber is and then very buttery in the long nose/tail" [35] 121. On-snow feel: "A lot of stability underfoot and all that nose/tail made it feel very forgiving for a full camber board" [35] 122. Park/Air: "More of a mountain freestyle board than a park board" due to long nose and tail [35] 123. Turning: "Lots of boards turn well, but this would be up there as one of the nicest" [27] 124. Uneven terrain: "Very easy to turn through bumps but not good for powering over them unless you are a lighter rider" [35] 125. Chatter in chop: "A lively board, so you'll get chatter in chunder" — low dampening [33] 126. Dampness: Board lacks dampness; "doesn't have a ton (or any?) of dampness" [33] 127. Reviewer concern: "If you're primarily riding gnarlier terrain or choppy conditions then I'd recommend something less lively and with a little more beef to it" [33] 133.
